newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: IHC Caland sees pft in new tunnel method.
newsitem.headline: IHC Caland sees pft in new tunnel method.

text.p: Shipbuilding and engineering group IHC Caland NV said on Monday it was part of a consortium testing a cheap, new tunnelling method which could be a substantial earner for the company.

"It is a new system and could prove rather profitable, but we don't want to be too excited before the results of the tests," company director Sjef van Dooremalen told a news conference after the announcement of IHC's 1996 results.
The new system involves setting the concrete wall of the tunnel during the drilling process, he said.
"Normally, the drilling has to stop. This method is cheap because the drilling can continue," Van Dooremalen said.
The results of the study project, 50 percent financed by the Dutch state, were due around the end of this year, he said.
The two leading companies in the consortium are IHC Caland and the unlisted port activities firm Heerema.
If the method proves viable, the consortium plans to build a traffic tunnel at the Wilhelmswerf in Rotterdam.
Van Dooremalen said although the method was suitable only for soft ground, he could see worldwide applications.
"The main concentrations of population are at deltas -- soft ground. These are also areas where tunnels are often needed because of the lack of space," he said.
Earlier, the company reported final net profits of 93.2 million guilders in 1996 and said it expected to see healthy growth to around 110 million in the current year.
